source_preparation: Three new ordinary source initializations, 500 epochs; then one 900-epoch full-correct single-generator preparation per source using the existing forward-only v3 protocol. All four predictor arms freeze and share that prepared encoder, both original affine maps, and readout. This tests capacity conditional on a relation-trained encoder, not spontaneous discovery.
predictor: Frozen original affine first map plus two-layer residual. Identity versus GELU between identically sized Linear(128,256), Linear(256,128); identical initial weights and zero final layer. Both have exactly 65920 trainable parameters. Second operator is unchanged and never refitted.
loss: Correct frozen first-state output-distribution KD in all four arms, plus full-space first-state MSE divided by fixed correct-target per-coordinate variance. Wrong geometry uses a complete derangement preserving all three gold visible answers. No composite labels, states, losses, checkpoint selection, or early stopping in fitting.
primary_prediction: The nonlinear correct-minus-wrong collision AB accuracy advantage exceeds the corresponding linear advantage.
uncertainty: Paired two-way bootstrap of three source clusters and 128 shared collision pairs, 10000 draws. Per-source contrasts reported; only three independent source initializations, so intervals are descriptive and limited.
test_policy: All twelve fixed-budget predictor fits and all three frozen-source preparations must finish before any new compound test inference. Known-only validation curves do not select checkpoints. A failed known-only source gate is reported without dropping or replacing its seed.
novelty: Exclude both previously examined matrix test orbit sets from the entire new study. New train/validation/test whole-group orbits are disjoint. Historical training orbits can recur under newly initialized models; no global never-seen-input claim.
scope: Prospective matched-parameter first-operator capacity-by-correspondence intervention; single-step supervision only. Correct/wrong teacher outputs, starts, exposures, initialization, fixed second operator, encoder, readout and update schedules are identical within a source. Supports can overlap across sources. No claim that a three-gold-answer collision ceiling limits access to full logits or hidden states.
